minutes.headline: Commission recommended the town not exercise interest in acquiring two tax-title Hollis Road properties.
minutes.summary: A routine but heavy Conservation Commission agenda: the board approved or continued roughly twenty wetlands hearings (mostly the Lake Shirley/Round Road subdivision lots, Pine Grove Road, Flatill Road, Ruth Street, Summer Street), ratified a tree-removal determination, and worked through an enforcement violation at 715 Reservoir Road requiring 11 replacement trees. Administrative business included approving a small shed-repair expenditure from the Hollis Road fund, agreeing the commission is not interested in the town acquiring two tax-title Hollis Road parcels, and starting work on raising the commission's fee schedule.

budget_items.topic: Hollis Road shed roof repair materials
budget_items.what_was_said: A member proposed buying shingles, nails and construction bags to finish the unfinished front section of the shed roof at 123 Hollis Road, with the cost to come from the fund dedicated to maintaining the Hollis Road structure.

Members said the department budget has become hard to follow after being merged with the land-use department amid finance-staff turnover, and asked the incoming finance director to attend the next meeting to explain it before FY27 begins.

A member said the commission should raise its fees so applicants share more of the town's legal/review costs; the agent said fee changes require rewriting bylaw and charter language and she will meet counsel in June, aiming for a fall town meeting warrant article.

transfers.description: Shed roof repair materials at 123 Hollis Road, drawn from the Hollis Road ("Haw") maintenance fund

decisions.decision: Chair duties for the administrative/business portion of the meeting were handed from Richard Burch to Jenny Putra.
The new finance director will join the May 20 meeting at 6:45 p.m., 15 minutes early, to walk through the conservation budget.
The conservation agent will meet town counsel in June to draft updated fee-schedule bylaw/charter language, targeting a fall town meeting warrant article.
The commission agreed in principle to let the pollinator habitat use the vacant side of the Hollis Road shed for tools, formalized by a later vote.
National Honor Society student volunteers will be used to help strip and re-shingle the Hollis Road shed roof and possibly mow the property.

what_happened.line: Commission voted to tell the Select Board it has no interest in the town acquiring two tax-title Hollis Road parcels.
Ordered replacement trees and erosion stabilization at 715 Reservoir Road over a wetlands violation, with daily fines if not completed.
Began work toward raising the commission's fee schedule, which needs new bylaw language and a fall town meeting warrant article.
Approved or continued roughly twenty wetlands permits across town, mostly subdivision lots on Round Road and several Flatill/Cross Road projects.
Asked the incoming finance director to walk the board through the conservation budget before FY27, after it became hard to follow post-merger with land-use.

why_it_matters: The Hollis Road recommendation feeds a Select Board decision on whether the town keeps or disposes of those tax-title parcels.
A higher conservation fee schedule would shift more of the town's legal and review costs onto permit applicants, but it requires a town meeting vote before taking effect.
The budget-clarity request signals a service whose FY27 costs residents may not be able to track clearly until the finance director explains the current structure.
